title: England has the best audience in the world
summary: Visiting yearly since about 1965, he says English listeners come to listen, throw out noisy people and follow him year after year.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, you really started your yearly stop about '65---
Yeah - but that seemed to go back--
I think you've gone every year since '65 - just about.

Well, I think actually - to tell you the truth, I think I'm better known in England than I am in America. I really mean it; Just that every place I go to it's sort of a fan thing for me. I stay at peoples houses and they're just--- I think-- I can safely say that I think the American-- the English audience is the best audience in the world.
By that you mean most enthusiastic or most appreciative--

And, I once was playing in a place - just to show you what was happening --- in a place where the audience had to stand up; there were no seats. There was just a bar and a big room. And, everybody huddles in there and stands in fron t of theband and, so, while we were playing, some guy got a coughing spell and they threw him out. (Laughter). Yeah, they really told him leave because they really -- you don't hear any rowdiness. You don't hear clicking of glasses and everybody talking loud; you don't hear that and

if somebody makes a disturbance- out they go. Because, you know, first of all, it costs a lot for those people to come to a jazz concert; they come to listen - they want to hear us. And, so, I don't know any place that I'm as well known as England. All of my records have been released in England - even the Danish ones have been released in England. And, so, It seems like every year I go back, I have more and more of a following-----
You get the same audience - a lot of the same people coming to hear you play---

Yes, I've got guys my age coming in on canes and crutches and wheelchairs and God knows what--- yeah. So, well, anyway, I just wanted to tell you about England because England is really a worthwhile place to play. Now, uh, when we're talking about---
